title: Split completed feature history from the active queue
acceptance_criteria: Keep feature_list.json as a compatible array for current work and load ordered optional progress/feature-history/*.json arrays before it. Every resulting staged file remains at most 20000 bytes.
Preserve all prior feature definitions and ordering exactly; validate IDs, terminal archive statuses, historical pins, and evidence across the combined queue.
State, review binding, and delivery consume the shared combined queue; missing archives remain compatible with fresh adoption and malformed supplied archives fail closed.
Focused regressions cover split and unsplit queues, duplicate IDs across files, nonterminal or malformed archives, latest approval selection, and unchanged historical pins.
Document archival and adoption rules, obtain independent review and passing verification, and commit the accumulated hook, small-code lane, and queue split without bypassing the hook.

title: Add a trivial lane and drop duplicate progress evidence
acceptance_criteria: A trivial change (at most 3 files and 30 added plus deleted lines, no work-item, progress, harness-test, dependency, configuration, CI, or riskyReview path) passes review binding without a work item, judged against the actual comparison base; an unconfigured risk policy refuses the lane.
Branch-level dependency maintenance and low-risk documentation keep passing after earlier trivial merges; every other untracked change still fails as REVIEW_BINDING_STALE.
pnpm run check:trivial-change reports eligibility and refusal reasons before an agent commits to the lane.
Harness state no longer requires progress/history.md entries or a progress/current.md plan; queue status, reports, and review binding remain required for normal work.
Docs and the PR template describe the trivial lane with PR-body evidence; focused tests cover eligibility limits, risk paths, base-relative maintenance, and the removed requirements.

title: Prototype an invoking-agent workflow with local inventory tools
acceptance_criteria: A local CLI lets the invoking agent start, inspect, edit, check, hand off, review, finish, and clean an inventory repair session without model API calls or credentials.

Session state survives separate command invocations. Editing is allowed only before handoff; handoff requires a successful current implementer check, and completion requires a current reviewer check and digest-bound approval plus final validation.

Input and session identifiers are validated, state writes are atomic, concurrent operations fail clearly, and invalid state or stale evidence cannot report success. Cleanup removes only the selected session.

Focused tests cover the command lifecycle, rejected transitions, invalid input, stale evidence, rejection and repair, cleanup, and concurrent access. Demonstrate the workflow with the invoking agent and an independent reviewer.
Documentation supplies a copyable agent prompt and command examples, explains usage limits and the local trust boundary, and records the existing repository delivery gate as the approval authority.
